problem.text: The routing projection inherited Linear's 128-feature padding, although its output is interpreted directly as expert scores without trimming to num_experts.

reasoning.text: Setting pad_to=1 preserves the router's exact hidden-size input and num_experts output dimensions. It fixes the projection boundary rather than adding a slice before softmax.

impact.text: Expert projections retain their existing padding. Router dtype, top-k selection, weight renormalization and execution-path selection are unchanged.

source_notes.text: Issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” reports Cholesky failure; issue #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” reports a sliced-weight loading size mismatch. Their relevance is only inferred shared-file context through linear.py; neither report establishes motivation for this router change.

limitations: No repository tensor operations, GPU kernels or end-to-end model workflows were executed; the computation checks integer dimensions only.
No model-specific accuracy or performance improvement is established.

chapters.title: Keep routing dimensions equal to the expert count

claims.text: Linear rounds each dimension using (dimension + pad_to - 1) // pad_to * pad_to. The default 128 is an alignment multiple, not an expert-count limit; 1 makes this rounding an identity.

The FP16 loading path passes the rounded dimensions to tensor loading, and LinearFP16.forward allocates and returns out_features columns without removing padding. BlockSparseMLP then applies softmax and top-k across every returned column, using the resulting indices for expert dispatch.

The likely correctness rationale is to exclude artificial routing candidates at their source. Exact router dimensions avoid both unnecessary projection columns and the need to mask or slice them downstream.

A standard-library transcription gives old/new output widths of 128/8, 128/64, 128/128 and 256/129 for illustrative expert counts 8, 64, 128 and 129. Counts already divisible by 128 have unchanged output width.
The earlier BlockSparseMLP entry records an all-expert fused-buffer cardinality mismatch.
That mismatch is carried over: the patch changes only router construction, while all-expert routing and fused allocations still use different expert counts under the recorded trigger.

findings.description: The router-padding fix leaves the inherited all-expert fused-path shape mismatch intact.
findings.trigger: One flattened token, fully EXL3 expert projections, activate_all_experts=True, and num_experts different from num_experts_per_tok.
findings.expected_behavior: Allocate for every selected expert or use the ordinary execution path.
findings.actual_behavior: Routing selects num_experts indices, but fused intermediates and outputs retain num_experts_per_tok entries. Whole-tree searches found Qwen3 MoE construction and decoder self.mlp.forward calls; inspected decoder calls pass params through. This establishes conditional reach, not that ordinary conversion triggers the single-token fused case.

verification.description: Compared routing cardinality with unchanged fused allocations and inspected decoder forwarding and Qwen3 MoE construction.
verification.limits: No native kernel execution or end-to-end reproduction.

verification.description: Modeled eight all-expert indices against a fused output expert dimension of two.
verification.limits: Integer shape arithmetic, not repository execution.

annotation.summary: Disables routing-gate padding so expert selection receives exactly num_experts scores; expert projection padding and the inherited all-expert fused-shape mismatch remain unchanged.

argv:
import json
print(json.dumps({'router_widths':[{ 'experts':n,'old':(n+127)//128*128,'new':(n+1-1)//1*1} for n in [8,64,128,129]],'all_expert_example':{'selected_indices':8,'fused_output_expert_dimension':2,'match':8==2}}))
